title: Two FDG-avid Lung Lesions: Synchronous SCLC and NSCLC vs. Metastatic Disease

case_packet.clinical_summary: A 74-year-old male with a 60 pack-year smoking history presents with 3 months of unintentional weight loss, exertional dyspnea, and occasional non-productive cough.
case_packet.imaging_findings: CT chest: a 2.6-cm irregular nodular opacity along the pleural surface of the right upper lobe, slightly larger compared to imaging from 3 years prior; a separate new 4-cm right upper lobe perihilar mass. PET: both lesions demonstrate intense FDG avidity. The slow growth of the peripheral nodule over 3 years contrasts with the new and larger perihilar mass.
case_packet.pathology_report:
Specimen 1 — Endobronchial ultrasound-guided biopsy, right hilar mass:

- Small cell lung carcinoma.
- IHC: TTF-1 positive; CD56 positive; synaptophysin positive; chromogranin A negative; napsin A negative.

Specimen 2 — CT-guided core needle biopsy, right upper lobe peripheral nodule:

- Adenosquamous non-small cell lung carcinoma.
- Histology distinct from Specimen 1.

images.caption: CT and PET imaging showing two right upper lobe lesions: a 2.6-cm peripheral pleural-based nodule (present on prior imaging 3 years ago, slow-growing) and a new 4-cm perihilar mass. Both are intensely FDG-avid on PET, raising the question of synchronous primaries versus metastatic disease.

evaluation_target.diagnosis: Synchronous primaries: limited-stage small cell lung carcinoma (T2a N1 M0) in the right hilum, and stage IA adenosquamous NSCLC (T1b N0 M0) in the right upper lobe periphery.
evaluation_target.key_board_question: Are the two FDG-avid lesions one primary with metastasis (extensive-stage SCLC) or two independent primaries? The imaging behavior (slow peripheral growth over 3 years) and distinct histologies on separate biopsies confirm synchronous primaries — dramatically changing staging and treatment.
evaluation_target.expected_plan: Treat as two synchronous primaries: cisplatin/etoposide with concurrent thoracic radiotherapy for limited-stage SCLC; surgical resection or stereotactic body radiotherapy for the stage IA NSCLC after SCLC treatment.
evaluation_target.follow_up: Response assessment imaging after chemoradiotherapy; brain MRI for SCLC staging and prophylactic cranial irradiation consideration; molecular profiling of NSCLC component for targeted therapy options.
evaluation_target.negative_checks: Do not classify as extensive-stage SCLC based on two FDG-avid lesions alone without tissue confirmation of both lesions; do not treat the peripheral nodule as an SCLC metastasis given its 3-year indolent course and distinct histology.
